children: , the social media and consumer AI company, drew a higher $875 price target from Jefferies as its Muse assistant gained early traction. Shares are up about 1.8% from Tuesday's $736.60 close.

Jefferies lifted its target from $710, leaving about 16.8% upside from the chart price. Muse can work through tasks in its own cloud browser and asks users to approve sensitive actions, including purchases. Meta offers a free version alongside paid plans, giving it a direct way to test whether early interest turns into revenue.

The chart puts Meta's $749.35 share price 12.38% below its $855.23 GF Value. That gap looks tempting, but downloads alone will not close it. Investors need evidence that people keep using Muse and pay for it, while Meta navigates the outside marketplaces its shopping features depend on.

title: Meta Gains 1.8% as Jefferies Reprices the Muse Opportunity
